newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian business sees more telecom competition.
newsitem.headline: Australian business sees more telecom competition.

text.p: Australian businesses expect increased competition and lower cost in the local telecommunications sector following full industry deregulation next month, according to a survey released on Tuesday.
The NUS Telecommunications Deregulation Survey said it found businesses also expect improved services after deregulation, which officially starts on July 1.

"Some 25 percent of companies surveyed believed deregulation would increase competition in the market and consequently reduce the cost of their telecommunications services," NUS International director Reuben Dobson said in a statement.
"However, only 20 percent expect deregulation will bring improved service," Dobson said.

Dobson said the survey found that Australian businesses rate customer service in telecommunications amongst the most important issues and that it wanted more services, which included customised billing and responsive after-sales service.
"Many also expect a shake-out in the telecommunications industry as a result of deregulation," Dobson said.
He said 17 percent of those surveyed expect takeovers and mergers of telecommunications companies and a reduction in the number of service providers.

The A$20 billion Australian telecom market is dominated by government owned Telstra Corp, which holds a near monopoly on the local call market and is main rival in the long distance market is Optus Communications Pty Ltd.
